provenance.quote:
Shall the City of Omaha be authorized to issue
and sell general obligation bonds in the amount of
one hundred fifty-five million and no/100 dollars
($155,000,000) for the purpose of providing funds
for payment of the cost of acquiring, constructing,
improving, equipping and rehabilitating police
buildings and facilities, fire stations, branch
libraries, park maintenance facilities, auditorium
support facilities, arena and convention center
facilities, public works storage facilities and city
wide building renovations and replacements
and other public facilities of the City of Omaha,
the approximate cost to the taxpayers of the
City of Omaha if this proposal is approved to be
one hundred fifty-five million and no/100 dollars
($155,000,000) plus interest payable on said
bonds to be paid from the fund for principal and
interest payments on the indebtedness of the City
of Omaha as proposed in the notice of election
which also provides that the approval of this bond
issue will not incur any increases in the debt
services tax levy rate of the City of Omaha over
the levy increase approved in 2020?

Shall the City of Omaha be authorized to issue
and sell general obligation bonds in the amount
of thirty million and no/100 dollars ($30,000,000)
for the purpose of providing funds for payment
of the cost of various park and recreation
improvement projects of the City of Omaha, the
approximate cost to the taxpayers of the City of
Omaha if this proposal is approved to be thirty
million and no/100 dollars ($30,000,000) plus
interest payable on said bonds to be paid from the
fund for principal and interest payments on the
indebtedness of the City of Omaha as proposed
in the notice of election which also provides that
the approval of this bond issue will not incur any
increases in the debt services tax levy rate of the
City of Omaha over the levy increase approved
in 2020?

contests.title: Valley — Sales tax allocation for municipal pool

provenance.quote:
A vote “YES” in favor of the Proposition will
authorize the City of Valley to allocate up to 50%
of City sales tax revenue for the construction and
related costs of a new municipal swimming pool
and aquatic facility, while maintaining the City’s
current plan to replace all critical water mains in
four years.

A vote “NO” opposed to the Proposition will
require all of the local sales and use tax to
continue to be allocated to water improvement
and wastewater improvement projects.

Shall the City Council of the City of Valley,
Nebraska, be authorized to allocate up to fifty
percent (50%) of the revenue the City collects
from its one and one-half percent (1.5%) local
sales and use tax, on and after January 1,
2027, for the purpose of planning, designing,
constructing, equipping, financing, and
maintaining a new municipal swimming pool
and related aquatic facilities?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes $155 million in general-obligation bonds for police and fire facilities, branch libraries, park maintenance, auditorium support, arena and convention facilities, public works storage and other city buildings. Repayment includes interest. The ballot says approval would not increase the debt-service tax levy rate beyond the increase approved in 2020.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this bond issue.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes $30 million in general-obligation bonds for city park and recreation improvements. Repayment includes interest. The ballot says approval would not increase the debt-service tax levy rate beyond the increase approved in 2020.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this bond issue.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows up to half of the revenue from the city’s existing 1.5% sales and use tax to support planning, construction, equipment, financing and maintenance of a new municipal pool and related aquatic facilities, starting January 1, 2027.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Allow up to half of this existing tax revenue to support the pool and aquatic facilities.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep all of this local sales and use tax revenue allocated to water and wastewater improvement projects.
